title: Sebastian and the Alibi
premise: Odile Okonkwo, a true-crime podcaster famous for closing every case they touch, reopens the 1994 disappearance of Marisol Vance, a small-town librarian whose diary was found with entries written after the date she vanished. As Odile digs, the diary begins describing Odile's own investigation with unsettling accuracy, suggesting someone is feeding it entries now to steer the case. Unraveling thirty-year-old alibis, Odile discovers Marisol faked her disappearance to escape a powerful judge and has been hidden in plain sight by a quiet found family — but the judge's heir, facing exposure, is hunting her still. In the climax Odile must choose between broadcasting the truth and protecting Marisol, and the ending sees justice served outside the law: the diary's final entry, written by Marisol herself, closes the case on Odile's terms.
about_author: Quentin Eastwick is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent two decades transcribing small-town trials before turning to fiction. Their novels are known for procedural precision, unreliable documents, and quiet characters who refuse to stay quiet.

chapters.title: The Coldest Case on Record
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Introduces Odile's podcast, their perfect record, and the fan letter containing Marisol Vance's diary — with entries dated after her 1994 disappearance. Odile, intrigued and arrogant, accepts the case. Beat: confident curiosity masking a hunger to stay undefeated.

chapters.title: Entries That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Forensic examination of the diary confirms the paper and ink span decades; the post-disappearance entries are genuinely old. Someone knew in 1994 that Marisol was alive. Beat: the thrill of an impossible puzzle.

chapters.title: Hollow Creek Welcomes You
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile arrives in the fading mill town of Hollow Creek, where Marisol vanished. The town is polite, closed, and watched. A judge's portrait still hangs in the diner. Beat: unease beneath small-town charm.

chapters.title: The Librarian's Card Catalog
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile visits the library Marisol ran and meets Ruth, Marisol's elderly assistant, who has kept Marisol's desk untouched for thirty years. Beat: grief preserved like a shrine; first hint of a protector.

chapters.title: Alibi One: The Judge
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile reviews Judge Ambrose Calloway's airtight 1994 alibi — a charity gala with fifty witnesses — and finds the guest list was curated by his clerk. Beat: suspicion of a constructed story.

chapters.title: The Diary Speaks Back
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A new entry appears in the diary describing Odile's arrival in Hollow Creek, written in Marisol's hand on old paper. Odile is being watched — or guided. Beat: fear and fascination entwined.

chapters.title: Alibi Two: The Husband
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Marisol's husband Dale, now remarried and prosperous, alibis with a fishing trip. Odile notices his hands shake when the diary is mentioned. Beat: guilt or fear? The reader can't tell.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Found the Diary
chapters.summary: Tobias's POV, a teenage letter-writer who discovered the diary in his late grandmother's attic. He's frightened; someone searched the attic after he mailed it. Beat: innocence colliding with danger.

chapters.title: Calloway's Heir
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Judge Calloway is dead, but his son Marcus, now district attorney, politely warns Odile off the case over coffee that feels like an interrogation. Beat: power wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV flashback to 1994: the night Marisol came to her terrified, holding documents about the judge. Ruth helped her disappear and has lied ever since. Beat: loyalty as burden.

chapters.title: The Gala Photograph
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile tracks down an unedited gala photo: the judge left for forty minutes, and the clerk who vouched for him later died in a car crash. Beat: the alibi begins to crack.

chapters.title: Podcast Pressure
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile's producer pushes to air early; sponsors circle; Odile refuses to broadcast until the case is closed — their rule, their identity. Beat: pride sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Entry: 'He Is Closer Than You Think'
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The diary warns Odile by name now. Odile sets a trap at their motel and catches a figure fleeing — Marcus Calloway's investigator. Beat: paranoia takes root.

chapters.title: Dale's Second Story
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Confronted with the gala photo, Dale admits he lied in 1994 — not about the fishing trip, but about what Marisol told him the week she vanished: that she was afraid of the judge. Beat: a marriage built on complicity.

chapters.title: The Attic Search
chapters.summary: Tobias's POV. Someone ransacks Tobias's home; his grandmother's letters are gone. He calls Odile, who realizes the diary was one of several documents Ruth's circle scattered for safekeeping. Beat: the found family's network revealed in fragments.

chapters.title: Alibi Three: The Sheriff
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The 1994 sheriff, now in a care home, recites a rehearsed statement — then, lucid for a moment, whispers that Marisol 'went where the river keeps its secrets.' Beat: a witness half-buried in his own lie.

chapters.title: The River House
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile finds an abandoned river house with fresh footprints and a tin box: medicine, a woman's reading glasses, recent. Someone lives out there — or did, very recently. Beat: hope and dread in equal measure.

chapters.title: Marcus Makes His Move
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus learns Odile found the river house and orders his investigator to burn it, framing the fire as vandalism. He tells himself he's protecting his father's legacy. Beat: self-justified corruption.

chapters.title: Ashes and Fingerprints
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The river house burns overnight. In the ashes, a melted locket engraved 'To M, with all my courage — R.' Ruth's. Beat: the protectors are exposed; the clock is now loud.

chapters.title: Ruth Disappears
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Ruth doesn't open the library. Odile finds her home cleaned out — she's gone to ground, or been taken. The diary's newest entry: 'She is safe. You must be brave now.' Beat: the stakes turn personal.

chapters.title: The Podcast That Started It
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile discovers a rival true-crime podcaster covered the Vance case in 2019 and was threatened into silence — his raw interviews still exist. Beat: Odile realizes they're not the first, and humility arrives.

chapters.title: Entry: 'You Were Never Supposed to Find Me'
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The diary entries shift tone — angrier. Odile begins to suspect the entries aren't warnings from Marisol but manipulation by whoever holds her. Beat: the guide may be the threat.

chapters.title: Tobias Runs
chapters.summary: Tobias's POV. Frightened after the break-in, Tobias flees town with the one document he kept hidden: a 1994 letter from Marisol to Ruth describing the judge's crimes. Beat: a kid carrying an adult's war.

chapters.title: The Dead Clerk's Widow
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile finds the dead clerk's widow, who confirms her husband forged the gala alibi under pressure — and left a sealed letter 'for whoever finally asks.' Beat: the legal record itself was the crime.

chapters.title: The Sealed Letter
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The letter names the judge's victims, the sheriff's payoff, and — stunningly — that Marisol wasn't fleeing the judge; she was gathering evidence against him when she vanished. Beat: the case inverts; Marisol was the investigator.

chapters.title: Alibi Four: Odile's Own
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Marcus publicly names Odile as a person of interest in the river house arson, turning the town and Odile's audience against them. Beat: the hunter becomes the hunted; isolation.

chapters.title: Where the River Keeps Its Secrets
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Following the sheriff's riddle, Odile finds the river's old ferry crossing and a hidden cellar beneath the ferryman's ruin — stocked, lived-in, decades of careful life. Beat: Marisol was never far.

chapters.title: Marisol
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Thirty years compressed: the judge's threats, Ruth's plan, the ferryman's cellar, the diary she kept writing to leave a trail for whoever was brave enough. Beat: relief and terror — the truth has a face.

chapters.title: The Diary's True Author
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol reveals the recent entries were hers — written to test whether Odile was Calloway's creature or a genuine seeker. The warnings were real: Marcus has been hunting her since his father's death. Beat: trust, hard-won.

chapters.title: Ruth in the Crosshairs
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Marcus's investigator grabs Ruth to draw Marisol out. Odile must decide: expose everything now and risk Marisol, or play Marcus's game. Beat: the podcaster's rule — never take a case you can't close — meets its cost.

chapters.title: The Trade
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile offers Marcus a trade: the sealed letter for Ruth, recording everything. Marcus agrees too easily. Beat: dread of the double-cross.

chapters.title: Double-Cross at the Mill
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge at the derelict mill. Marcus takes both Ruth and the letter and plans to burn the mill with all evidence inside. Beat: trap sprung; lowest point.

chapters.title: The Town Decides
chapters.summary: Hollow Creek's POV in chorus — Dale, the sheriff's daughter, the widow, Tobias — as they converge on the mill, each carrying their thirty years of complicity and choosing, at last, to stand. Beat: found family as a town.

chapters.title: Fire at the Mill
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The mill burns a second time; this time the town saves the evidence, and Odile saves Ruth, while Tobias livestreams Marcus's confession to the assembled crowd. Beat: chaos turning to reckoning.

chapters.title: Marcus Unraveled
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Exposed — his investigator flips, the forged alibi surfaces, the livestream spreads — Marcus bargains, then breaks, revealing where his father's remaining files are hidden. Beat: power's corruption devouring its heir.

chapters.title: The Files in the Courthouse Wall
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Behind the courthouse wall: Marisol's original evidence, enough to posthumously indict Judge Calloway and reopen every case he tainted. Beat: justice, thirty years late, arriving anyway.

chapters.title: The Case Odile Couldn't Broadcast
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile faces the choice: air the episode and make Marisol a fugitive target forever, or close the case in silence. Odile chooses Marisol, releasing the evidence to prosecutors instead and ending the podcast arc unrecorded. Beat: pride surrendered for principle.

chapters.title: A Desk Untouched No More
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Marisol, publicly declared a victim of Judge Calloway who fled and died, quietly returns to Hollow Creek under a new name. She and Ruth reopen the library together. Beat: homecoming, understated and warm.

chapters.title: The Final Entry
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol writes the diary's last entry herself and gives it to Odile: 'Case closed. Thank you for asking.' Odile's perfect record stands — but differently than before. Beat: peace after pursuit.

chapters.title: Sebastian and the Alibi
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Odile's POV. Odile reveals the title's meaning: Sebastian was the ferryman who sheltered Marisol — the quietest alibi of all. Odile starts a new case, humbler now, with Tobias as their researcher and the town behind them. Beat: found family forged; the next story begins.
